questions.q: Before cleaning, how should hinged instruments such as clamps be placed?
options: Closed and locked to protect the tips
Closed and held with a rubber band
Open, in the unlocked position
Under the heaviest items in the basket
questions.explain: Box locks, serrations and jaws can only be reached by brushes, water and detergent when the instrument is open. Locked instruments trap soil in the hinge, which then survives cleaning and blocks sterilization.

questions.q: Why should soiled instruments be kept moist from the point of use until cleaning?
options: Moisture sterilizes them on the way
Dried blood and soil are much harder to remove
Wet instruments are lighter to transport
Dry instruments set off the washer alarm
questions.explain: Soil that dries on instruments sticks to surfaces and in lumens and is far harder to clean. Point of use care removes gross soil and keeps items moist, for example with a product made for that purpose, until they reach decontamination.

questions.q: How does an ultrasonic cleaner remove soil?
options: Cavitation: tiny bubbles form and implode on the surface
High heat that melts the soil away
Steam under pressure
A chemical that sterilizes the surface while it soaks in the tank
questions.explain: Sound waves create tiny bubbles that collapse against the instrument and loosen fine soil from crevices and hinges. Ultrasonic cleaning comes after gross soil is removed and does not disinfect or sterilize the items.

questions.q: Under the Spaulding classification, an item that enters sterile tissue is what kind of item?
options: Semi-critical, so high-level disinfection is enough
Non-critical, so low-level disinfection is enough
Non-critical, so cleaning alone is enough
Critical, so it must be sterilized
questions.explain: Spaulding sorts items by the risk of infection from their use. Critical items enter sterile tissue or the vascular system and must be sterile. Semi-critical and non-critical items need high-level and low-level disinfection respectively.

questions.q: An item that touches mucous membranes or non-intact skin is classified as what?
options: Critical
Non-critical
Semi-critical
Environmental surface
questions.explain: Semi-critical items contact mucous membranes or broken skin without entering sterile tissue. They need at least high-level disinfection, and sterilization is preferred when the item can tolerate it.

questions.q: A blood pressure cuff that only touches intact skin falls in which Spaulding class?
options: Critical
Non-critical
Semi-critical
Implantable
questions.explain: Items that touch only intact skin are non-critical. Intact skin is an effective barrier, so cleaning and low-level disinfection are enough for them.

questions.q: How should an instrument be brushed in the sink to limit aerosols?
options: Under the surface of the cleaning solution
Above the water line, quickly
Under hot running tap water
In the air, then dipped in the sink
questions.explain: Brushing below the waterline keeps splashes and aerosols that carry microorganisms in the sink. Brushing above the surface or under running water spreads contaminated droplets toward the technician and the room.

questions.q: Why must detergent be diluted exactly as its instructions for use say?
options: Stronger solutions always clean better
Dilution only changes the smell
The dilution only sets the sterilization time for the next step
A wrong dilution leaves soil or residue and harms instruments
questions.explain: Detergents are tested at the dilution and temperature their manufacturer states. Too weak, soil stays behind; too strong, residues remain and some instruments can stain or corrode. Measuring tools and automatic dosing exist for that reason.

questions.q: Which personal protective equipment is expected for manual cleaning in decontamination?
options: Clean scrubs, a hair cover and closed shoes, nothing more
A lab coat and safety shoes
Fluid-resistant gown, gloves, and face and eye protection
A surgical mask alone
questions.explain: Manual cleaning can splash blood, body fluids and chemicals. A fluid-resistant gown, gloves suited to the task and face and eye protection guard the skin, eyes, nose and mouth, as the bloodborne pathogens rules require.

questions.q: Which federal rule requires employers to protect workers from exposure to blood and body fluids?
options: The FDA device labeling and registration rule
The OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard
The HIPAA privacy rule
The CMS billing rules
questions.explain: OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030, requires an exposure control plan, protective equipment, training, sharps safety and hepatitis B vaccination offered to exposed workers, which covers decontamination staff.

questions.q: Why is biofilm a problem in instrument reprocessing?
options: It shields microorganisms from cleaning and disinfection
It makes instruments shine after drying
It only forms on brand new instruments before their first use
Sterilization alone always removes it
questions.explain: Biofilm is a layer of microorganisms held in a sticky matrix on wet surfaces, especially inside lumens. It protects them from detergents and disinfectants, so prompt and thorough cleaning that prevents it from forming matters.

questions.q: How is the cleaning performance of a washer disinfector checked?
options: By weighing the load after the cycle
By the color of the detergent
By listening to the spray arms turn and timing the full cycle
With a cleaning test run as the IFU and policy require
questions.explain: Washers, ultrasonic cleaners and cart washers are checked with efficacy tests at the frequency set by the manufacturer's instructions and department policy. The results are documented, and a failed test means the equipment is checked before further use.

questions.q: A single-use device arrives in decontamination mixed in with a reusable set. What should happen to it?
options: Clean it and add it back to the tray
Sterilize it twice to be safe
Discard it or route it as policy says, never reprocess it
Return it to the vendor without a label or a record of the case
questions.explain: Single-use devices are not designed to be cleaned and sterilized by the facility. They are discarded or, if the facility has a contract, sent to an approved third-party reprocessor under its policy.

questions.q: Which water is generally used for the final rinse of critical devices?
options: Utility tap water only
Critical water, treated to remove contaminants
Water from the hand washing sink, filtered through a clean towel
Water collected from the ice machine
questions.explain: Water quality is matched to each step. Utility water is used for flushing and washing, while the final rinse of critical and semi-critical devices uses critical water, treated so that it does not leave microorganisms, endotoxins or minerals behind.

questions.q: What is the minimum effective concentration (MEC) test of a reused high-level disinfectant for?
options: Confirming the solution is still strong enough to use
Measuring the temperature of the solution in the soaking basin
Counting how many items were soaked
Setting the exposure time
questions.explain: Reusable high-level disinfectants weaken with use and dilution. The test strip checks that the concentration is still above its minimum before use, at the frequency in the instructions; a failed test means the solution is discarded and the result is recorded.
